dominant_variable: Whether pandemic-era demand represented durable recurring connected-fitness economics or a temporary pull-forward that left excessive fixed cost, inventory and valuation behind.
business_thesis: Historical analogue only: Peloton shows how exceptional demand can be misread as a permanent growth rate. The useful lesson is to separate installed-base economics and subscription retention from hardware demand pulled forward by an external shock.
counter_thesis: A high-quality subscription layer and strong brand could have supported durable value if hardware demand normalized gradually and fixed costs, inventory and supply-chain capacity had been kept flexible.
market_expectation_assessment: Retrospective reconstruction, not a contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation. The 2020-2021 price and operating plan capitalized a continuation of extraordinary hardware demand; FY2022 results showed the embedded growth assumptions were not durable.
valuation_framework: Historical analogue: compare equity value and revenue expectations at the growth peak with normalized post-pull-forward connected-fitness revenue, subscription gross profit, FCF and net liquidity. Do not annualize shock-driven hardware demand.
kill_criteria: Hardware demand normalizes while capacity and inventory remain sized for peak demand.
Subscriber growth and engagement fail to offset hardware gross-margin deterioration.
Valuation continues to require pandemic-era growth assumptions after demand normalization.
unresolved_evidence_gaps: Exact contemporaneous sell-side expectation distributions are not fully persisted.
No original TRQuant 2020-2021 recommendation is asserted; this is a 2026 historical analogue.

provenance.note: historical analogue created in 2026; not evidence of contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation
